articles.name: A conversation displays an automated resolution but it was escalated to an agent
articles.title: A conversation displays an automated resolution but it was escalated to an agent
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

A conversation in an email escalated to an agent, but it shows an automated resolution. An escalation shouldn’t be an automated resolution. What happened?

Resolution steps

From your description of the behavior, the conversation isn’t an email interaction. It’s a messaging conversation, handled by the AI agent.

The AI agent attempted to escalate the conversation to a human agent, but no agents were available to accept the handoff. For this reason, the escalation couldn't complete. Instead, the bot created a ticket for follow-up and then finished the conversation itself.

This explains why you see both elements:

  • Custom resolution: Escalated to agent — because the bot reached the escalation step and attempted the handoff
  • Conversation status: Automated resolution — because no human agent actually joined the live messaging conversation, so it ended with the bot

While labels can look contradictory at first, labels describe two different parts of the same flow. In this case, it appears to be a failed handoff or no-agents-available scenario in messaging, rather than an email case or a successful live escalation to an agent.

articles.name: Can I prioritize the use case resolution with AI agents and emails?
articles.title: Can I prioritize the use case resolution with AI agents and emails?
articles.body:
Question

With a double intent in emails with an AI agent, can we prioritize the order of my use case resolutions?

Answer

No, there isn't a way to prioritize the resolution with more than one or multiple use cases.

  • The AI agent will try to solve as many use cases as your settings allow.
  • In addition, the AI agent will only start the next use case if the customer asks for it.

articles.name: Announcing new guided onboarding for Copilot auto assist
articles.title: Announcing new guided onboarding for Copilot auto assist
articles.body:
We’re happy to announce that turning on and getting value from Copilot auto assist got much simpler thanks to guided onboarding. In three steps you can: 

  • Select knowledge sources available to auto assist
  • Decide who has access to auto assist and turn it on
  • Review and publish AI-generated procedures that will ground auto assist in your business processes

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

For new and existing users of auto assist, guided onboarding will be available in Admin center. After the first admin in a given account completes the onboarding, it will no longer be available on that account.

What do I need to do?

Whether you're an existing user of auto assist or you haven’t used it yet but wanted to try it, go to Admin center and follow the three guided steps. See Turning on and configuring auto assist to learn more.

Note: Remember that to see auto assist suggestions on tickets you must tag the desired tickets with the agent_copilot_enabled tag to indicate to auto assist that it should be active on these tickets. If you're participating in the updated auto assist experience EAP, then this doesn't apply to tickets that use the Based on confidence suggestion mode..

articles.name: How can I update the phone number field of a user with AI agents and API?
articles.title: How can I update the phone number field of a user with AI agents and API?
articles.body:
Question

How can I update a user's phone number field? I can't achieve that with update_user.

Answer

The phone number is a field on a customer object. It is not tied to user identity. You can update this with the Update User API endpoint, which is a custom API call from your AI agent with Integration or action flow.

If you want to change the phone number in the user's profile, you can also use this method to update the user's phone number.

articles.name: Announcing enhancements to the agent status picker in the Agent Workspace
articles.title: Announcing enhancements to the agent status picker in the Agent Workspace
articles.body:
Zendesk is pleased to introduce new customization options for the unified agent status picker. Admins can now hide statuses agents don't need and reorder statuses to align with agent workflows.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Admins can now customize which unified agent statuses are available in the status picker for agents to select as well as the order in which statuses appear.

Hiding unified agent statuses

It is now possible for admins to hide any custom unified agent statuses and the standard Away and Transfer only statuses. Hiding a status removes it from the status picker in Agent Workspace, but doesn't delete the status or change its routing configuration. 

Hiding statuses can also help admins prepare custom statuses in advance and keep them hidden until they're ready to be used.

Note that the standard statuses of Online and Offline can't be hidden and are always visible in the status picker.

Reordering unified agent statuses

On the Agent statuses page in Admin Center, admins can now drag and drop statuses into the order in which they will be displayed in the status picker. After the changes are saved, the updated order is reflected in the Agent Workspace.

Custom statuses can be restricted to specific groups, but their position in the status picker follows the global order on the Agent Statuses page.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Businesses with complex workflows often create multiple custom statuses to help agents manage their availability, time, and workload. As the number of statuses grows, agents may need to scroll through a long list to find the correct option. These changes make the status picker easier and more efficient for agents to use because it ensures the status picker reflects options relevant to current business workflows, removes unnecessary choices without deleting their configuration, and allows admins to place the most frequently used statuses at the top of the list.

What do I need to do?

No action is required. Existing statuses will remain visible and keep their current order unless an admin chooses to hide or reorder them. To take advantage of these new features, see Managing the unified agent statuses available to your agents.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Announcing improvements to the Copilot similar tickets feature
articles.title: Announcing improvements to the Copilot similar tickets feature
articles.body:
Zendesk is introducing an improved version of similar tickets, a feature in the Copilot add-on that helps agents find and reuse solutions from previously solved tickets.

The updated experience finds more relevant tickets across all languages and channels, helping agents resolve customer issues faster and with greater confidence.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Similar tickets now uses a hybrid retrieval model that combines keyword and semantic matching:

  • Keyword matching finds tickets with exact terms, such as product names and error codes.
  • Semantic matching finds tickets about the same issue even when the issue is described using different words.

The feature also considers the ticket subject, description, and first meaningful comments to understand the current issue. It suggests recently solved or closed tickets from the previous 90 days, helping agents find solutions that reflect your current products, workflows, and policies.

With this update, the similar tickets feature:

  • Supports all languages and channels.
  • Provides suggestions for more tickets.
  • Finds more relevant past solutions, including when customers describe similar issues differently.
  • Doesn't rely on intelligent triage topics or entity classification for ranking.
  • Doesn't rely on generative AI to find similar tickets.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

The improved similar tickets feature helps agents find relevant past solutions more consistently, including when customers describe the same issue differently or contact you through another language or channel. This helps agents resolve tickets faster and provide more consistent support.

What do I need to do?

No action is required if similar tickets is already turned on. Agents will see the improved suggestions automatically. Keyword matching is available immediately, while semantic matching can take from a few hours to one week to become fully available.

To learn more, see Turning on similar tickets. 

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Announcing collapsible call transcripts and summaries for Zendesk Voice
articles.title: Announcing collapsible call transcripts and summaries for Zendesk Voice
articles.body:
We're excited to announce a new formatting option for call transcripts and AI summaries in Zendesk Voice. Admins can now choose to display transcripts and call summaries as collapsible comments instead of internal notes, helping reduce ticket clutter from lengthy call transcripts and summaries.
This feature is available to Zendesk Voice customers with the Copilot add-on. 

This announcement includes the following topics: 

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

When Show call transcripts on tickets is enabled, admins now have two format options:

  • Add transcript and summary as internal notes (default): Continues to add transcripts and summaries as internal notes.
  • Add transcript and summary as collapsible comments: Displays transcripts and summaries as collapsible comments that agents can expand when needed.

The new collapsible format helps maintain ticket readability, especially for longer calls that generate extensive transcripts. And, just as with internal notes, these collapsible comments are always private.

Important: Manual redaction is not available for collapsible comments. If your workflow requires agents to manually redact text from call transcripts or summaries, use the internal notes format.
Note: Automatic redaction of PII and PCI data from call transcripts continues to work with both formats.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Lengthy calls can generate extensive transcripts that make tickets harder to scan and make it more difficult for agents to review ticket history and previous interactions.

With collapsible transcript formatting, teams can:

  • Maintain ticket readability: Keep tickets easier to scan while preserving access to the full transcript and summary.
  • Improve agent efficiency: Review ticket history and customer context without scrolling through lengthy transcripts.
  • Preserve transcript value: Continue leveraging transcripts for AI processing, compliance, and quality assurance.
  • Keep transcripts available: Use collapsible comments to reduce ticket clutter without disabling transcript display.

What do I need to do?

No action is required. The existing internal notes format remains the default. To use collapsible comments, update your call transcription settings. The setting applies to transcripts and summaries of future calls. Existing transcripts and summaries remain in their original format.

For more information about call transcription options, see Call transcription and summarization FAQ.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Announcing new action builder connectors
articles.title: Announcing new action builder connectors
articles.body:
Zendesk is excited to introduce two new action builder connectors for ClickUp and Magento 2, helping teams automate workflows across project management and ecommerce operations.

This article includes the following sections:

  • What's changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What's changing?

Zendesk is introducing new connectors for ClickUp and Magento 2 in action flows. These connectors help teams connect support workflows with the tools they use to manage projects, collaborate across teams, and support ecommerce customers.

ClickUp Connector

With the ClickUp connector, teams can create and update tasks, add comments to tasks, search for tasks, and retrieve information about ClickUp lists, users, and spaces. This helps support teams turn customer issues into trackable work items for product, engineering, operations, or other internal teams. For example, a workflow can create a ClickUp task from a Zendesk ticket, update a task when ticket details change, or add a comment to keep internal teams informed as the customer conversation progresses.

Magento 2 Connector

With the Magento 2 connector, teams can search for and look up ecommerce information directly in action flows, including customers, orders, products, invoices, and shipments. Teams can also create new customer accounts. This gives agents and admins more context when handling commerce-related requests, such as checking order details, reviewing shipment information, validating product data, or finding customer records as part of a support workflow.

Together, these connectors make it easier to automate work across support, project management, and ecommerce systems without requiring manual handoffs between tools.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Customer service teams often need to coordinate with teams and systems outside Zendesk to resolve requests quickly. These new connectors help teams:

  • Create and update project tasks from support interactions
  • Keep customer issues connected to internal follow-up work
  • Bring ecommerce customer, order, product, invoice, and shipment context into workflows
  • Reduce manual data entry and context switching
  • Improve collaboration between support, operations, ecommerce, product, and engineering teams

By expanding action flows to more business systems, Zendesk helps teams build more connected, efficient workflows that support faster and more informed customer service.

What do I need to do?

These connectors are being rolled out to all accounts with access to action flows. For more information, see 
Understanding the action builder and action flows.

articles.name: Announcing WhatsApp business-scoped user IDs in Zendesk and the Sunshine Conversations API
articles.title: Announcing WhatsApp business-scoped user IDs in Zendesk and the Sunshine Conversations API
articles.body:
We're announcing the general availability of WhatsApp business-scoped user IDs (BSUIDs) in Zendesk and the Sunshine Conversations API.

This release enables Zendesk to support WhatsApp users who are identified by a BSUID instead of a phone number as Meta rolls out WhatsApp username functionality.

This announcement answers the following questions:

  • What’s changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What’s changing?

Zendesk now supports WhatsApp BSUIDs for customers using WhatsApp with Sunshine Conversations.

With this release:

  • BSUIDs can appear in Sunshine Conversations API responses and events.
  • WhatsApp client records can use BSUIDs as part of the updated user identity model.
  • Zendesk can process messages from WhatsApp users whose phone number is unavailable and who are identified through a BSUID.

Meta controls the rollout and availability of WhatsApp username functionality, which may vary by country.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Meta is changing how WhatsApp users are identified as part of its rollout of WhatsApp usernames. Supporting BSUIDs ensures Zendesk can continue processing WhatsApp conversations when users are identified by a BSUID rather than a phone number.

What do I need to do?

If you use custom APIs, webhooks, Marketplace apps, or workflows that depend on WhatsApp phone numbers or user identifiers, see Business-scoped user IDs in the WhatsApp BSUID migration guide and complete any required tasks.

If you've already made the required changes described in the migration guide, no further action is needed.

If you use Zendesk's standard WhatsApp integration without custom integrations or custom code, no action is required. Zendesk will handle the transition automatically.

For more information, see the WhatsApp BSUID migration guide.

If you have questions about this announcement, visit our community forum, where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Service Incident - August 7, 2026 - Support | All Pods - Exchange connector not retrying outbound emails
articles.title: Service Incident - August 7, 2026 - Support | All Pods - Exchange connector not retrying outbound emails
articles.body:
Summary

On July 23, 2026, from 10:14 UTC to August 7, 2026, 13:32 UTC, Exchange Connector customers across multiple pods experienced delayed or missing outbound Support email notifications. Failed email sends were not retried as expected, and in some cases, pending retries prevented subsequent ticket notifications from being sent.

Timeline

August 7, 2026 10:35 UTC | August 7, 2026 3:35 AM PT

We're aware of an issue affecting email retries in our Exchange connector. Our engineering team is currently investigating and working on a resolution. We'll provide updates as soon as we have more information.

August 7, 2026 15:49 UTC | August 7, 2026 8:49 AM PT

We are happy to report that the issue affecting email retries in our Exchange connector has been resolved, and the backfill for affected emails has completed. Any missed retried emails during the window of impact should be processed, and now appear as expected. Thank you for your patience during our investigation.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a software change that unintentionally prevented the process responsible for retrying failed outbound emails from running. As a result, failed email deliveries were not automatically retried as expected.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, we restored the process responsible for scheduling failed email retries and introduced safeguards for messages that were no longer eligible for retry. The fixes were gradually deployed across production, and missing email-status notifications were backfilled for affected messages that could not be retried.

Remediation Items

  1. Introduce monitoring to alert us if automated retry actions fail to start.
  2. Investigate the possibility of adding extra email context to improve clarity.
  3. Consider merging all service roles into a single operational unit for better performance.
  4. Develop a process for extended tests to verify the system’s long-term stability.
  5. Examine strategies to ensure one individual ticket does not become entirely unresponsive.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Parameters are missing in an API Order Status use case
articles.title: Parameters are missing in an API Order Status use case
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

When using an API Order Status use case, some parameter values may appear in the API call configuration but fail to populate during the conversation. In some cases, only one parameter is collected while the remaining required values are missing, which prevents the order status workflow from triggering correctly.

Resolution steps

A common cause is that multiple API integrations were created for the same Order Status check. If one of those integrations requires more parameters than the bot collects in the Order Status use case, the workflow may fail and only some values may populate. Misconfigured or missing API parameters can also contribute to the issue.

To resolve the issue:

  • Review the API integrations configured for the same Order Status check
  • Remove any duplicate API integration that is conflicting with the intended setup
  • Confirm that the remaining API integration includes the correct required parameters
  • Verify that the bot is collecting every parameter needed by the Order Status use case
  • Test the flow again to confirm that all parameter values populate and the API triggers successfully

If the issue was caused by a duplicate integration requiring additional parameters, deleting that duplicate integration should allow the correct values to populate as expected.

To learn more API integrations in AI agents, see About the integration builder for AI agents.

articles.name: Converting tickets to service requests
articles.title: Converting tickets to service requests
articles.body:
When the service catalog is turned on for a brand, agents can convert tickets into service requests when they are associated with a service catalog item. When a service is set for a ticket, the ticket's form, fields, and requirements are updated to the applicable service request form. This allows agents to convert requests received through other channels, such as email or web form, into service requests.

What's my plan?
All Suites Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

When the service catalog is turned on for a brand, agents can convert tickets into service requests when they are associated with a service catalog item. When a service is set for a ticket, the ticket's form, fields, and requirements are updated to the applicable service request form. This allows agents to convert requests received through other channels, such as email or web form, into service requests.

This article contains the following topics:
  • Considerations when converting tickets to service requests
  • Converting tickets to service requests
  • Converting a service request to a ticket
Related articles:
  • Adding services to your service catalog
  • Submitting service catalog requests

Considerations when converting tickets to service requests

All tickets associated with brand that has a service catalog turned on include a Service ticket field. Requests submitted through the service catalog are automatically created with a service request form, but requests submitted through other channels use ticket forms by default. Adding a value to a ticket's service field, either manually or with a business rule, converts a ticket to a service request.

When the ticket form changes to a service request form associated with the selected service, the following things happen:
  • The ticket displays the fields configured for the selected service.
  • Values are retained for fields that are present on both forms.
  • Required fields on the service request form must be completed before the ticket can be saved.

A service request can be converted to a ticket by removing the value in the service field.

You can't convert closed requests from tickets to service requests or vice versa.

Converting tickets to service requests

Tickets are converted to service requests by adding a value to the ticket's service field. This can be done automatically, with triggers, or manually by agents. See:
  • Automatically adding a service to a ticket
  • Manually adding a service to a ticket

Automatically adding a service to a ticket

To use triggers to automatically add a service to a ticket, use the Service > Service action.

To automatically add a service to a ticket
  1. Create or edit a ticket trigger.
  2. Under Conditions, specify one or more qualifications the ticket must meet to be converted to a service request.
  3. Under Actions, click Add action and select: Service > Service | Service catalog item, where Service catalog item is replaced with a service from your service catalog.

    The the service specified in the action statement's Value field is the value that is added to the ticket's Service field.

Manually adding a service to a ticket

If an agent is working a ticket and determines it needs to be converted to a service request, they can manually add the service to the ticket as long as it has a status of new, open, pending, or on-hold.

To manually add a service to a ticket
  1. In Support, access a ticket.
  2. In the ticket properties panel, under Service, select the service being requested in the ticket.
  3. Review the fields on the service request form to ensure all required fields contain values.
  4. Save your change by clicking Submit as and selecting the appropriate status.

Converting a service request to a ticket

Deselecting a service from a ticket's service field removes the association between a ticket and the service catalog item and converts it back to a ticket form.

To manually remove a ticket's service value
  1. In Support, access a ticket and set the Service field to an empty value.
  2. Save your change by clicking Submit as and selecting the appropriate status.

articles.name: Linking directly to comments in a ticket
articles.title: Linking directly to comments in a ticket
articles.body:
As an agent, you often need to reference a specific update, decision, or customer reply in a long ticket conversation. You can create links to connect directly to specific comments within a ticket and share it with others. Comment links make it easier to share the exact context with teammates, collaborate on complex requests, and reduce the time spent searching through ticket histories.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

As an agent, you often need to reference a specific update, decision, or customer reply in a long ticket conversation. You can create links to connect directly to specific comments within a ticket and share it with others. Comment links make it easier to share the exact context with teammates, collaborate on complex requests, and reduce the time spent searching through ticket histories.

This article contains the following sections:

  • About ticket comment links
  • Creating and sharing ticket comment links

Related articles:

  • Adding comments to tickets

About ticket comment links

Using a Copy link option within a ticket, you can copy a direct link to a specific ticket comment and share it with others. When someone clicks the link, the link opens the ticket, navigates to the referenced comment, and highlights it for easy reference.

Comment links follow Zendesk’s existing ticket access permissions:

  • Users can access a linked comment only if they have permission to access the ticket.
  • Sharing a link does not grant additional access to a ticket or its comments.
  • Redacted comments remain linkable and can still be located in a ticket.
  • If a linked comment has been deleted or is no longer available, Zendesk will handle the link without exposing unavailable content.

Typical uses for sharing comment links include:

  • References from one ticket to another
  • Links shared within the same ticket conversation
  • Slack or other internal messaging tools
  • Emails
  • Documentation tools such as Google Docs
  • Internal notes or collaboration workflows

The Copy link option is available for comments in:

  • Tickets from all channels, except Chat.
  • Tickets that aren't archived.
  • Tickets created on or after January 1, 2026

Creating and sharing ticket comment links

To share ticket comments links, you can copy the link directly from a ticket comment and paste the link into another document, another ticket, or another location within the same ticket.

To create and share a comment link

  1. In a ticket, locate the comment you want to share.
  2. Click the options menu icon () next to the comment.

  3. Select Copy link from the options menu.

    The comment link is copied to your clipboard and you’ll see a confirmation message.

  4. Paste the link into another location, wherever you want to include the ticket comment link.

To open a comment link
  • Click the comment link.

    The link opens the associated ticket in Support, scrolls to the referenced comment, and highlights it.

Summary

August 5, 2026 00:09 UTC | August 4, 2026 5:09 PM PT

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was triggered by the deployment of a new release before all necessary pre-deployment checks had been completed. An issue with our documentation process meant that some important resources weren’t published as planned, leading to temporary service startup problems on one of our systems, which resulted in 503 errors. To fix this issue, we first reverted the Lotus deployment to quickly restore service to Z2 on Pod 26. We also removed version 30400 from our main release channel to ensure that this issue does not occur again.

We are pleased to inform you that the issue affecting access to the Zendesk Support platform has been resolved. We appreciate your patience and understanding while our engineering teams worked diligently to resolve this issue.

This incident occurred after we made a change to adjust our system's processing settings. As traffic increased in the EMEA region, the system became more reactive, prioritizing some processes over others. This shift reduced our overall capacity to serve requests, which in turn resulted in temporary service interruptions and the appearance of HTTP 503 errors.

To resolve the issue, we increased our Classic app-server fleet from 118 to 194 instances, thereby alleviating bottlenecks in our processing queue. We also reversed the recent resource allocation change that had been contributing to increased preemption pressure. Additionally, we instituted a strict policy requiring all future nodegroup rollouts to occur exclusively within the approved deployment window.

  1. Review and adjust our deployment criteria to prevent system saturation and high error rates during node transitions.
  2. Enforce specific maintenance windows for all service switchovers to ensure smooth transitions.
  3. Evaluate increasing the baseline capacity for Tier One Core Services to at least nine units to enhance performance.
  4. Implement a grace period of five minutes before initiating any resource adjustments to allow ongoing tasks to complete.

articles.name: Workflow: Capture a customer’s name and email in an AI agent and sync it to Zendesk tickets
articles.title: Workflow: Capture a customer’s name and email in an AI agent and sync it to Zendesk tickets
articles.body:
AI agents can collect a customer's name and email during a messaging conversation and pass that information to Zendesk when a ticket is created. This is useful when customers start a conversation as anonymous users and you want the resulting ticket to include their details.

This article provides two workflow options:

  • Collect customer details with a customer message block
  • Collect customer details with a form in an AI agent message

In both workflows, you use an Update user action to write the customer's name and email to the Sunshine Conversations user profile before the ticket is created.

Before you start

Before setting up this workflow, make sure that:

  • You're using an AI agent with messaging
  • You have permission to create or edit AI agent flows and actions
  • You understand your account's messaging email identity settings

If you want to associate messaging users with existing Zendesk users before the conversation starts, you also need end-user authentication for messaging using JWT, which requires developer implementation.

Option 1: Use a customer message block

Step 1: Add message blocks to collect the customer's name and email

Add customer message blocks in the flow before the escalation step. Use one block to ask for the customer's name and another to ask for the customer's email address.

Configure each block to save the customer response as a parameter so you can reuse the values later in the flow.

Example:

  • Ask for the customer's name and save it to a parameter such as name
  • Ask for the customer's email address and save it to a parameter such as email

After the values are collected, reference them in later blocks using the parameter format:

  • {{name}}
  • {{email}}

Step 2: Pass the saved values during escalation

When the flow reaches the escalation path or a specific downstream block, create an action and pass the saved parameter values using the parameter formats {{name}} and {{email}}.

Using the double angle bracket {{}} format ensures the stored parameter values are passed correctly.

Option 2: Use a form in an AI agent message

Step 1: Add a form to the AI agent message

Create or select a form template that collects the customer's name and email, then add that form to your AI agent message.

Add the form template to connect it to the relevant flow or escalation path.

Step 2: Verify the parameter names

Then run a test conversation and review the session data to confirm the exact parameter names created by the form. Check the conversation log for the test conversation and review the session parameters ensuring they are set from the template form.

Step 3: Create an Update user action

Create an action for Sunshine Conversations that updates the user profile.

Map the form's saved parameter values to these user fields:

  • givenName = {{name}}
  • email = {{customerEmail}}

The parameter names in the action must exactly match the ones saved by the form.

Step 4: Add the action with the Escalation

Add the Update user action in the escalation block or in the relevant AI agent configuration so it runs before the ticket is created.

This links the collected form details to the Sunshine Conversations user profile before the ticket is generated.

Understand how email identity settings affect the ticket requester

Whether the collected email appears on the Zendesk ticket depends on your messaging email identity settings.

  • If your account allows unverified emails, the email collected by the AI agent can be added as a user identity and used as the ticket requester
  • If your account allows only verified emails, the collected email won't be used as a trusted identity unless the user is authenticated and the email is verified
  • In unauthenticated conversations where only verified emails are allowed, the ticket may appear as a conversation with a web user instead of showing the collected email address

To learn more about email identities see Understanding and setting up end-user authentication for messaging.

If you want to identify customers against existing user profiles before the conversation starts, use JWT-based end-user authentication for messaging. This requires developer implementation or help from Zendesk Professional Services.

Summary

Between July 31, 2026, 01:15 UTC and August 4, 2026, 09:11 UTC, some customers with Employee Service Suite accounts and sandboxes experienced an issue that unexpectedly removed their Ultimate (AI Agents Advanced) entitlement. As a result, affected customers were temporarily unable to access AI Agents Advanced until the issue was resolved and access was restored.

Timeline

August 3, 2026 6:34 UTC | August 2, 2026 11:34 PM PT

We are investigating an issue where a small number of accounts lost access to AI Agents (Ultimate) on Friday, July 31st at approximately 1:20 AM UTC due to a provisioning process error during an Employee Service Suite update. The affected product is AI Agents Advanced. We are working to restore the access in of the known affected accounts in priority and are implementing safeguards to prevent this from happening again. We continue to investigate the full scope of impact and will provide further updates as soon as it becomes available.

August 3, 2026 11:38 UTC | August 3, 2026 4:38 AM PT

We have successfully resolved the issue affecting AI Agents access. All identified accounts have had their access restored. The AI Agents service is now fully operational for all affected customers.

August 4, 2026 9:30 UTC | August 4, 2026 2:30 AM PT (Issue recurrence for some accounts)

We’ve identified additional accounts that lost access to AI Agents as part of the provisioning issue reported earlier. Our engineering team has completed work to restore access for these accounts, and all identified affected accounts should now have their AI Agents access restored.
We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience while we worked to resolve this issue.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by an incomplete Unleash provisioning and exclusion list used during the Employee Service Suite backfill. Consequently, eligible accounts that should have been excluded were inadvertently processed, resulting in the unintended cancellation of Ultimate (AI Agents Advanced) entitlements.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, the Account Service and Unleash teams restored Ultimate access for all identified affected accounts. They also updated the exclusion list to include impacted and at-risk accounts, preventing unintended entitlement removals during future billing events and synchronization processes. Additionally, accounts that had been incorrectly included in the rollout were removed from the rollout scope to prevent recurrence.

Remediation Items

  1. Share a validated list of all affected accounts with stakeholders before starting any corrective updates.
  2. Require peer review and cross-team approval before performing account removals.
  3. Include the Advocates Team in early communications for visibility into planned changes.
  4. Align with all relevant teams on the rollout plan before executing corrective actions.
  5. Investigate the omission of subscribed accounts from the update process and implement safeguards to prevent similar gaps in future rollouts.

articles.name: Using live call transcripts in Zendesk Talk
articles.title: Using live call transcripts in Zendesk Talk
articles.body:
You can use the transcript to review what has been said and search for details to check information during the call without interrupting the conversation. You can also use real-time suggestions during the call, seeUsing real-time AI suggestions for voice calls.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

Summary: ◀▼

Live call transcription gives you a real-time text transcript during voice calls, with speaker labels, timestamps, and auto-scrolling updates. You can review what’s been said, search for keywords or phrases, switch transcription language during the call, and check details without interrupting the customer. It also supports multilingual transcription for common languages.

Zendesk Suite customers must also have the Copilot add-on to use this feature.
If your admin has turned on live call transcription, you have access to a real-time text version of a voice call while the conversation is in progress. The transcript shows speaker labels (Agent or Customer), timestamps from the start of the call, and automatically scrolls to show the most recent conversation.

You can use the transcript to review what has been said and search for details to check information during the call without interrupting the conversation. You can also use real-time suggestions during the call, see Using real-time AI suggestions for voice calls.

To use live transcripts during an ongoing call

  1. In the ticket call controls, click Show transcript ().

    The transcript panel opens in the ticket, below the controls, showing the most recent part of the conversation and updates automatically as the conversation continues.

  2. Click the expand icon (v) in the upper-right corner of the transcript panel to access the whole conversation.

    The transcript auto-scrolls to show the latest conversation.
  3. (Optional) Scroll up and down to review the whole conversation.
  4. (Optional) Click Scroll to latest at the bottom of the panel to access the current conversation.

  5. To find a specific topic, search in the upper-right corner of the transcript panel and enter a keyword or phrase.

    It's a case-insensitive search that supports partial matches. This allows you to jump to relevant parts of the conversation and check specific details. For example, information about an "account", "order" or "error message".

    The transcript highlights all instances of the search term. If there are multiple matches, use the arrows to move between matches.

  6. (Optional) In the language menu, select the language you want to use for transcription.

    The transcript language defaults to your Zendesk profile language. You can change the language during an active call to match the language the customer is speaking. The transcript uses the new language for ongoing transcription. Previously transcribed text is not retranscribed.

    You can also select the multilingual language option to seamlessly switch between the following languages only: English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Russian, Portuguese, Japanese, Italian, and Dutch.

  7. Click Hide transcript () to close the transcript panel.

    Ending the call also closes the transcript panel.

  • Fixed an issue where agents were sent into a redirect loop when opening Support from the product tray on a host-mapped help center belonging to a secondary brand.


Help Center

New:

  • Copenhagen theme: The Help Center API now supports creating and deleting user subscriptions, so you can follow and unfollow a user programmatically instead of only through the help center UI.

Fixed:

  • Lisbon theme: Fixed an issue where articles the AI agent referenced in a conversation would not open for accounts using Essential AI Agent 
  • Articles containing a dynamic content placeholder that no longer resolves now render instead of returning an error.

Web Crawler

New:
  • You can now create up to 50 web crawlers per account, up from the previous limit of 20. This allows you to sync and index content from more external sources without needing workarounds.
Fixed:
  • Fixed an issue where web crawlers would fail with "Page fetch failed" errors when the URL extraction service was temporarily unavailable, preventing content from being incorrectly purged during transient service issues.

Mobile SDK's

New:

  • The SDK is now fully compatible with Android 17, aligning with the latest updates and platform requirements from Google.
  • Following a change introduced in Android Gradle Plugin 9.0, applications integrating the SDK must now use the same or a higher compile SDK version. This release requires compileSdk 37. This requirement does not affect the consuming app’s target SDK version. Learn more in the AGP 9.0 release notes.
  • The Android Gradle plugin was updated from 8.13.2 to 9.2.1

Fixed:

  • Fixed an issue where the navigation bar buttons on Xiaomi devices had poor contrast, improving visibility for the SDK's UI elements.

Apps and integrations

New:
  • Guardrails (Support) (paid)
    • Guardrails helps you enforce brand standards, workflow rules, and quality expectations inside the Zendesk agent experience before costly support mistakes happen. Tailor each guardrail carefully based on ticket attributes and agent changes. Use flexible condition logic to define when a guardrail should run, including ticket fields, assignee status, group assignment, custom fields, user role, and more.
  • Lleverage (Support)
    • Lleverage is a low-code AI development platform that lets teams build visual workflows by connecting nodes on a canvas. Each node performs a specific function — AI generation, data processing, integrations — that can be chained together to automate business processes. Connect your Zendesk account to Lleverage and use your support data in AI-powered workflows. No code required.
  • SevenRooms Reservations (Support) (paid)
    • SevenRooms Reservations brings your restaurant's booking history directly into the Zendesk ticket sidebar, so support agents can see a guest's reservations without switching tools. The app looks up the ticket requester's SevenRooms reservation history by email and lets agents see upcoming and past reservations, plus pending reservation requests, at a glance. Open any reservation or request to view its full details, read-only. Search for any guest's reservations by email address and jump straight to the reservation in SevenRooms to make changes.
  • ManoMano Connector by Volvox (Support) (paid)
    • ManoMano Connector by Volvox connects your Zendesk Support instance with ManoMano to unleash the power of seamless order data retrieval from any ManoMano marketplace. Effortlessly retrieve order details directly from a ticket field, instantly view detailed billing and shipping information related to the ticket, and access comprehensive ordered product details with ease.
  • Attachment Preview & Export (Support) (paid)
    • Attachment Preview & Export allows you to preview attachments in tickets and export them easily. Files can be previewed in a modal or a separate tab, and downloaded individually or in bulk.
  • Ticket Field Update Restriction (Support) (paid)
    • Ticket Field Update Restriction restricts updates/modifications on ticket field. You can limit updates based on user roles and groups. An alert will appear in a popup window if restricted field(s) are edited. Changes will be discarded and fields will revert to their previous values.
  • Ticket Field Entry Requirement (Support) (paid)
    • Ticket Field Entry Requirement ensures public replies are only allowed when a specified value is entered in a specified ticket field during ticket updates. If the target field is empty or contains an incorrect value, public replies will be disabled. If the target field does not meet its condition, an alert will pop up when the update button is clicked.
  • Internal Note Attacher (Support) (paid)
    • Internal Note Attacher displays an internal note field on the sidebar of the ticket screen to help prevent accidental public replies. Press 'Comment' to copy your input into the internal note. You can also configure the 'Comment' button in settings to save input directly as an internal note.
  • CaseMargin (Support)
    • CaseMargin helps you read support tickets and write the brief an agent actually needs.  The brief builder lives in the ticket sidebar. One click reads the full conversation, comments, internal notes, requester history, and returns a structured brief: what's actually happening, what's already been tried, what the evidence shows, and what to do next. Nothing is invented. When the ticket doesn't have enough information to draw a conclusion, the brief says so.

articles.name: Troubleshooting two-factor authentication (2FA) issues for team members
articles.title: Troubleshooting two-factor authentication (2FA) issues for team members
articles.body:
When a team member signs in for the first time after the two-factor authentication requirement is turned on, they choose how to receive their verification codes. If they set up an authenticator app as their preferred two-factor authentication method, Zendesk Support will not send codes by email or SMS. In that case, they must enter the code generated by the authenticator app.

If they lose access to that app, they cannot sign in with email or SMS unless they later change their two-factor authentication method from their profile settings after regaining access.

To resolve this issue, select an option below:

If the team member uses an authenticator app

  1. Confirm which two-factor authentication method the team member selected when they first signed in
  2. If they selected an authenticator app, ask them to open that app and enter the current verification code
  3. Let them know that email or SMS codes will not be sent while the authenticator app is set as their preferred method

If the team member is locked out of their authenticator app

  1. Ask an admin to generate a temporary recovery code for the team member
  2. The team member can use that recovery code to sign in
  3. For detailed admin steps, See Getting recovery codes for team members locked out of their accounts

If the team member wants to change their two-factor authentication method

  1. After signing in, go to the user profile page
  2. Under Security settings > Two-Factor Authentication, select Manage to update the authentication preferences
  3. For the Preferred method, select Edit to switch from the authenticator app to another supported method, such as email or SMS, if available in the account configuration
  4. Save the changes and use the newly selected method the next time you sign in

Additional notes

  • The delivery method depends on the option the team member originally configured
  • Not receiving an email or SMS code does not always indicate a delivery issue
  • If an authenticator app is configured, the verification code must come from that app
  • An admin may need to assist with account recovery if the team member no longer has access to their device or app

Additional resources

  • Using two-factor authentication to sign in to Zendesk Support

articles.name: Can I use Segments with agentic AI agents for email?
articles.title: Can I use Segments with agentic AI agents for email?
articles.body:
Question

Can I use Segments with agentic AI agents for email? Segments are missing from my procedures. I do not see or find Segments under my Procedure. How and where can I add Segments?

Answer

Yes, you can use segments with email AI agents to target specific audiences.

  • However, Segments do not exist yet within your Procedure. For instance, you cannot use a segment inside a procedure to build a conditional branch.

Instead, you can target the expected audience with a segment by editing your use case directly:

  1. Edit your use case
  2. On the Edit use case details pop-up, use the Segments field > Save

articles.title: What's new in Zendesk: August 2026
articles.body:
Click Follow in the What's New section to be notified each month when the What's New is published.

Support

  • Automatic-refresh for views means your views are updated every minute without manual refresh, keeping sidebar counts and ticket tables current. Auto-refresh pauses during bulk actions to avoid interrupting selections, improving agent efficiency and data accuracy. See Accessing your views of tickets.
  • Service catalog requests on behalf of others allows authorized users to submit service catalog requests for other users, with the selected user becoming the requester, and the submitter added as a CC to track progress. Admins can turn on this feature account-wide and per service, improving accuracy in employee service workflows. See Adding services to your service catalog.
  • Custom field rendering update in the ticket sidebar limits the initial display to 50 custom fields for ticket forms with more than 70 fields, adding a Show more button to reveal the rest. This improves performance and usability without hiding any fields permanently. See Adding custom ticket fields to your tickets and forms. 
  • Organization-based asset targeting in the Asset Management side panel allows agents to switch context from the ticket requester to an organization, enabling management of shared and departmental assets directly from ticket workflows. This helps IT agents view, assign, and unassign organization-level assets without leaving the ticket. See Using and managing IT assets in ticket workflows.
  • Agents can use task events to view key task list and task-level actions, including when a task list was added, completed, or reopened, and when individual tasks were marked complete or incomplete. See Viewing task events for a ticket.
  • Improved messaging notifications for agents. See Using the notification list to manage conversations. 
    • Notification sounds: Agents will receive audio alerts for ticket updates, including updates to tickets that aren’t currently open in their workspace. This helps agents stay aware of new activity without needing to keep every ticket tab open.
    • Dynamic favicons: Agents will see a visual cue in the browser tab and a sound when there are new incoming ticket notifications. This gives agents another way to notice unread updates when they are working in another browser tab or with other applications. 
    • Mute notifications: Agents can mute notifications for a set period of time when they need focused, uninterrupted work sessions.

    • Reduced notification list clutter: The notification list will only show updates for unsolved tickets, helping agents focus on active work and reducing the number of updates they need to review.

  • IT asset panel user selection in the Agent Workspace now allows agents to select and manage assets for any user linked to an account without changing the ticket requester. This improves efficiency by reducing steps in multi-user asset scenarios. See Using and managing IT assets in ticket workflows.

AI agents

  • The AI agents migration introduces infrastructure changes for customers who purchased the AI agents - Advanced add-on before March 10, 2026, consolidating Zendesk help center connections, adding locale-scoping to search rules, and respecting article view permissions. Existing CSV imports remain usable, but new imports are temporarily unavailable. The Zendesk web crawler replaces the previous version, and more built-in connectors to external content sources are now available. Migration downtime within the AI agents will be brief, with temporary interruptions to messaging, email, and voice channels. See Announcing AI agents workspace migration and updates to knowledge and search rules.

Copilot

  • Copilot intelligent triage is now included in Suite and Support Professional plans and above, enabling automatic AI classification of incoming tickets by topic, sentiment, language, and entities at no extra cost. This helps identify ticket trends and provides AI-powered workflow recommendations. See Understanding Copilot AI features.
  • Auto assist now generates suggestions using content from external sources, such as Confluence, Notion, and web crawlers, as well as internal knowledge articles. This broadens the content pool for more comprehensive text suggestions. See Understanding auto assist sources for suggestions.

  • Auto assist now uses similar solved tickets as a knowledge source across all channels and languages when no procedures or articles are available. This enhancement provides agents with more relevant reply suggestions based on real-time resolutions, helping teams respond faster and deliver consistent support. Agents can also view the rationale and relevant tickets used for suggestions. See About auto assist.

  • Admin copilot users can get help directly from Launchpad. Admin copilot reviews your account and makes recommendations to improve your setup. Admin copilot recommendations appear at the top of Launchpad. See Using admin copilot with Launchpad.

Accounts and billing

  • The Zendesk Suite trial provides an AI-driven setup wizard to help you automatically set up your account. The setup wizard leverages information from your corporate website to customize your account, minimizing the time required to get you up and running.  See Using AI to automatically set up your Zendesk account. 

Security

  • If Zendesk detects suspicious activity, users may be signed out and redirected to the sign-in page. After signing in again, they’ll be returned to where they left off. See Understanding Zendesk session time.

People

  • Manage Zendesk Support apps is a new custom role permission that allows Enterprise plan admins to delegate app management tasks to specific team members without full admin access. This permission grants access to install, configure, and remove Support apps, enhancing security and operational efficiency. See Creating custom roles and assigning agents.

Knowledge

  • Accordions, callouts, and tabs have been added to the help center article toolbar. You can use these new components to structure and highlight content directly in the article editor without the use of custom code. See Using tabs to group content in the article editor, Using accordions to create expandable and collapsible sections in the article editor, and Using callouts to highlight content in the article editor. 

  • The following knowledge connectors are now available to connect as external knowledge sources to your Zendesk account. Content from external knowledge sources is available wherever external content is used.

    • Dropbox
    • Jira
    • Freshdesk
    • Contentful

    See Connecting external knowledge sources to your Zendesk account.

Contact Center

  • Live call transcription allows Contact Center agents to view real-time transcripts during voice calls, improving accuracy, productivity, and accessibility. Available for Zendesk Contact Center with Amazon Contact Lens. See Using live call transcripts.
  • The enhanced call transfer experience in the native Zendesk Contact Center now shows agents availability information for other agents and queues before transferring calls. This helps reduce failed transfers and customer wait times. See Transferring calls.
  • Auto-accept calls allows calls to be automatically accepted after about 2 seconds, removing the Decline button to prevent missed calls and improve efficiency. Admins can enable this per agent via Amazon Connect. See Configuring auto-accept and Automatically accepting calls.
  • Support for Jabra devices allows agents to control calls through the buttons on their Jabra headset making it easier to handle calls. See Setting up Jabra devices.
  • Browser notifications natively in Contact Center provide the call number in the notification of incoming calls and allow agents to test notifications through their voice settings. See Setting up browser notifications.
  • Agents logs allow your agents and Zendesk to better troubleshoot issues. See how to access logs.

Voice

  • Live call transcription allows Voice agents to view real-time transcripts during voice calls, improving accuracy, productivity, and accessibility. It supports speaker labels, searchable text, timestamps, language switching, and UI controls. Available for Zendesk Voice with Copilot add-on. See Using live call transcripts.
  • Voice ringtones now allows Voice agents to choose from 20 different ringtones and adjust the ringtone volume in the call console. Agents must be Away or Offline to change these settings. See Changing the ringtone.
  • Auto-accept calls now allows calls on phone lines (PSTN) to be automatically connected without ringing for agents to accept or decline. Admins can configure a delay of 0, 5, or 10 seconds before auto-accept to help agents prepare. This change aims to reduce missed calls and improve average speed to answer, enhancing customer satisfaction. See Managing phone line settings.

Workforce management

  • New permissions structure and greater granularity for teams in Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM) allow admins to configure permissions at a more granular level and, for the first time, grant read-only access to teams. Permissions are now organized into sections, each with top-level options and the ability to set custom permissions for each feature. See Understanding WFM roles and permissions.

Quality assurance

  • Multi-tiered root causes in Zendesk Quality Assurance (QA) introduces a cascading dropdown system that organizes root causes into up to three tiers. This makes it easier for reviewers to select the right root cause, reduces the time spent searching through extensive lists, and enables more granular and actionable quality insights. See Viewing and managing root causes for review scores.

Apps and integrations

  • Custom variables, loop steps, and enhanced retry logic for action flows introduces intuitive ways for admins to create and update variables, add looping steps, and customize retry logic per step, improving action flow complexity and resiliency. See create a new action flow and edit an existing one.
  • Additional action builder connectors are available for the following apps: ServiceNow, monday.com, Microsoft Planner, Azure DevOps, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Business Central, HiBob, Iterable, New Relic, and Snowflake. These connectors enable end-to-end automation, reduce manual work, and synchronize data across platforms. See Creating action flows to automate processes across Zendesk and external systems.
  • Step-level error handling and search in action builder introduces the ability to configure error handling for each step in action flows, allowing flows to halt or continue on failure with specific success or failure paths. It also adds keyword search for triggers and actions to simplify workflow setup. See Understanding the action builder and action flows and Creating action flows to automate processes.

Developer

  • API tokens removal is a phased discontinuation of API tokens as an authentication method for Zendesk Support APIs. Starting July 28, 2026, unused tokens will auto-deactivate, new token creation will be blocked from October 27, 2026, and all tokens will be permanently disabled by April 30, 2027. Customers must migrate integrations to OAuth for improved security. See Migrating from API tokens to OAuth access tokens in the Zendesk developer documentation.
  • The messaging Web Widget includes a new minimalistic styling preset and enhanced customization APIs for the conversation list and message log. This update offers a compact, modern chat UI with options to hide avatars, timestamps, previews, and bubble backgrounds. See Set Customization in the Zendesk developer documentation.

articles.name: Why do short agent activities display without full ticket details in real time?
articles.title: Why do short agent activities display without full ticket details in real time?
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

In Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM), short agent activity displays in real time without complete ticket data. These agent activities only last 1 to 30 seconds.

Resolution steps

Agent activities lasting between 1 and 30 seconds may occasionally appear without fully enriched ticket details. 

Cause

This issue arises because Zendesk WFM captures agent activity events, such as ticket updates, almost instantly from the time tracker. However, ticket metadata, including workstream assignment, tags, or status, is captured periodically from Zendesk services, which introduces a short and predictable delay.

When an agent’s action is extremely brief, Zendesk WFM may record the event before it retrieves the ticket metadata, which results in:

  • Incomplete enrichment: Some activities temporarily lack full ticket context, such as a missed workstream assignment
  • Apparent discrepancies: On-screen reports may show a brief misalignment between activity duration and ticket details, even though no data is lost

Zendesk WFM records every event thoroughly and later matches it with its ticket details. The result is a complete, accurate dataset, even if very short activities initially display without full enrichment.

Workarounds and recommendations

Zendesk recommends these approaches:

  • Data recalculation: If you observe discrepancies in activity enrichment, reach out to Zendesk customer support to request a recalculation on stored data
  • Manual updates: For cases where data appears outdated, update tickets manually to ensure workstreams and reports reflect the correct details

For more information, see: About the Agent activity page.

articles.name: Sometimes line-breaks aren’t included when I apply macros
articles.title: Sometimes line-breaks aren’t included when I apply macros
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

At times, line breaks and spaces don't appear when I use a macro. Sometimes the text formatting changes, and the pre-defined text or canned response removes line breaks and spaces. Occasionally, when I apply a macro, the line breaks and spaces don’t show up properly. I don't want my snippet or template to change in ticket responses to customers.

Resolution steps

Copy and pasted content

It's possible you copied content from another source and pasted it into your macro. This action results in incorrect formats in Zendesk.

Follow these steps instead:

  1. Recreate your macro from scratch, don't copy and paste any content

  2. Refresh your ticket page > click Apply macro and retry

Comment placeholders

In addition, using comment placeholders in macros can be inconsistent due to a known limitation in the following events:

  • When applied to a single ticket
  • When applied while bulk-editing a ticket
  • When applied while referencing a placeholder for multi-line or custom text fields

articles.name: Service Incident - July 23, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - [Jira v1] Field Sync Not Transmitting
articles.title: Service Incident - July 23, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - [Jira v1] Field Sync Not Transmitting
articles.body:
Summary

On July 23, 2026 from 20:42 UTC to 21:31 UTC , some customers using the Jira v1 integration experienced an issue where updates made in Jira did not appear in their linked Zendesk tickets. Other parts of the integration continued to work, but field updates were not completing as expected.
 

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a recent platform upgrade in the Jira integration service. During the update, an internal component it relied on was no longer available, which caused background tasks to stop completing properly. As a result, field updates were left unfinished. Because the issue happened behind the scenes, it did not produce clear signs of failure, which made it look like the updates were just stuck.
 

Resolution

To fix this issue, we returned the Jira integration service to the previous version that was working as expected. This restored normal processing and allowed updates to complete again. 
 

Remediation Items

To reduce the likelihood of this happening again, we are taking steps including:

  1. Improve alerting for silent job failures
    Add monitoring that detects when background jobs are failing without producing explicit errors or queue growth.

  2. Restore and strengthen integration smoke tests
    Re-enable Jira integration smoke tests with valid test accounts so field-sync failures are caught before production release.

  3. Add safer dependency upgrade checks
    Improve validation for framework upgrades to detect when removed methods or incompatible instrumentation could affect job processing.

  4. Enhance observability for field sync processing
    Add clearer metrics and logs for job pickup, completion, and failure states so stuck syncs can be identified sooner.

  5. Review SLO/SLI coverage for field sync behavior
    Ensure current reliability measurements capture silent failures, not just queue size or explicit error conditions.
     

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.
